title: The hammer in motion — do you see pieces now?
question: You asked: 'I don't see pieces coming off in chunks. Do you?' Honest answer on that still sheet: no, and I do not think you were wrong. This is the same swing animated. What I can see: a notch opens, joints part, and a few small angular lumps hop out and land. What I think is actually wrong is that a landed piece of stone is drawn as *stone* — the exact grey it came out of — so a chunk lying at his feet is invisible against the cliff. Do you want broken-off rock to read as a different colour once it lands (the way rubble already does), or is the problem the size and number of the pieces?
context_md: Counters, since the eye cannot get them off a grey-on-grey pile. On this cliff face one blow promotes roughly 13-45 cells as bodies and everything lands within 8 frames. I also quadrupled the throw a blow gives its fragments (fastest piece 1.07 -> 4.02 cells/frame) so they at least leave the wound. On a scene where pieces have somewhere to go -- an attached shelf worked with repeated blows, the second gif -- the same code gives 41 bodies, 1,498 cells promoted, 66% chunk by mass, sizes [1:40 2:28 3-5:31 6-7:7 8-15:4 16-63:2 64+:6]. So the mechanism does produce a distribution of pieces; on a flat wall at ground level they are small, they land immediately, and they are the colour of the wall.
